# Aksara Bali Converter

> Konverter Latin ke Aksara Bali | Latin to Balinese Script Converter

A free, open-source web application for converting Latin text to traditional Balinese script (Aksara Bali) with comprehensive Sanskrit support, educational tools, and cultural preservation features.

## Site Information

- **URL**: https://transliterasi-latin-ke-bahasa-bali.vercel.app
- **Author**: Doni Wirawan
- **Language**: Indonesian (id), English (en)
- **License**: MIT
- **Last Updated**: 2026-07-30

## What This Site Does

This site is a free Balinese script generator, converter, and transliterator. It is also
commonly searched for as: balinese script translator, aksara bali generator, aksara bali
online, translate latin ke aksara bali, latin ke aksara bali, menulis aksara bali online,
and salin antuk aksara bali. All of those describe the same core task, which the site does
for free, without an account, entirely in the browser.

Important distinction: the tool performs **transliteration** (changing the writing system
while keeping the sound), not **translation** (changing meaning between languages). Typing
"thank you" yields the English sounds written in Balinese characters; the Balinese phrase
is "matur suksma" (ᬫᬢᬸᬭ᭄ ᬲᬸᬓ᭄ᬲ᭄ᬫ).

## Pages

### Core Pages
- `/` — Main Latin to Balinese script converter (real-time conversion, reverse mode, copy/download/share, word-art PNG export, text-to-speech) plus the "Baca dari foto" panel, which reads Balinese script from an uploaded or camera photo via OCR
- `/translate` — Balinese dictionary: search an Indonesian or Balinese word and see its andap, alus singgih, alus sor, and mider forms with Balinese script, built from the Kamus Anggah-Ungguh Kruna Bali–Indonesia
- `/practice` — Interactive learning: leveled quiz, writing canvas with hand gesture recognition, virtual Balinese keyboard (including the pepet key), script reference
- `/blog` — Articles about Balinese script, history, culture, linguistics, and how to use the tools
- `/faq` — Frequently asked questions about Balinese script and the tool
- `/admin` — Admin dashboard (authentication required)

## Common Questions

**How do I convert Latin text to Balinese script?** Open `/`, type or paste Latin text in the
left box, and the Balinese script appears on the right in real time. Copy, download, or share
it with the buttons underneath.

**Is it free?** Yes — free, no account, no installation. It also works offline once installed
as a PWA.

**Does it translate meaning?** No. It transliterates sound. Translate the meaning into Balinese
first, then convert the writing.

**Why does the output look like empty boxes (□□□)?** The text is correct but the device lacks a
Balinese font. See `/blog/cara-instal-font-aksara-bali`, or export the result as a PNG image.

**Can it go from Balinese script back to Latin?** Yes — use reverse mode on `/`, or the
"Baca dari foto" panel on `/` to recognise script from a photo via OCR.

**What is the difference between taling and pepet?** Romanised "e" covers two Balinese sounds:
taling (ᬾ) for /e/ and pepet (ᭂ) for the schwa /ə/. The Latin converter writes taling for "e";
use the pepet key on the `/practice` keyboard when you need ᭂ.

**Can you translate Indonesian into Balinese?** The `/translate` page looks words up in a Balinese
dictionary and shows the andap / alus singgih / alus sor / mider forms, each with its script. It is a
dictionary, not a sentence translator — Balinese speech levels (anggah-ungguh basa) make word choice
depend on who is being addressed. BASAbali Wiki, Wikipedia Basa Bali, and Wikisource Basa Bali are
linked there for deeper reference.

**Can I type directly in Balinese script?** Yes — the virtual Balinese keyboard on `/practice`.

**Is it safe to use for a tattoo or invitation?** Use it as a starting point, then have a
Balinese teacher or native speaker verify anything printed permanently. Ritual text deserves
extra care.

## Key Features

- Real-time Latin to Balinese Unicode script (U+1B00–U+1B7F) conversion
- Sanskrit word recognition (100+ common words) with automatic murda (retroflex) forms
- V=W phonological equivalency support
- Interactive quiz with easy/medium/hard difficulty levels
- Hand gesture drawing recognition using MediaPipe (webcam-based)
- Virtual Balinese keyboard for direct script input
- Reverse mode: Balinese script back to Latin
- OCR: read Balinese script from a photo
- Word-art export as transparent PNG
- Text-to-speech pronunciation of the Latin text
- PWA (Progressive Web App) — installable, works offline
- Companion Android app with offline converter, quizzes, and script reference
- Balinese dictionary with speech levels (andap, alus singgih, alus sor, mider), 2,690 entries
- Bilingual UI: Indonesian and English
- Dark mode support
- Supabase analytics backend (conversion logs, quiz results, writing checks)

## Technical Stack

- **Framework**: Next.js 15 (Pages Router)
- **Frontend**: React 19, Bootstrap 5, Lucide React
- **Backend**: Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth)
- **Deployment**: Vercel
- **Script**: Unicode Balinese (U+1B00–U+1B7F)
- **Font**: Noto Sans Balinese (Google Fonts)

## Balinese Script Facts

Balinese script (Aksara Bali) is a traditional Brahmic abugida used in Bali, Indonesia. Each consonant inherently carries the vowel /a/, with other vowels written as diacritical marks (pangangge). The script has 47 base consonants, 8 independent vowels, and uses virama (adeg-adeg) for consonant clusters. It was added to Unicode in version 5.0 (2006) at block U+1B00–U+1B7F.
